annotations.text:
Ambient - the screen is a sky that follows the day: dawn peach, morning blue, dusk rose, night indigo. Try the timeOfDay chip.
For: a wall display is seen in passing, so the colour alone tells you roughly what time it is, and it is the most distinctive of the three.
Against: text sits on a shifting background, so contrast must be checked in every palette, and cards read softer than today.
Pi: one static gradient and solid tints, no blur.

Editorial - the morning paper: serif headlines, hairline rules, one lead story, photo-led features.
For: the most personality per pixel, and it reads beautifully up close.
Against: slower to scan from across the room than big cards, and it leans on good photos. The hatched blocks are placeholders; the app already pulls trip photos from Wikimedia and news images from the feeds, recipes would need a source.
Pi: flat colour and type only, the cheapest to render.

Bento - tiles of different sizes, colour-coded by kind, with soft depth from layered surfaces. Try the dark chip.
For: fastest to scan, big numerals read across the room, and it is closest to today's layout, so the easiest to migrate.
Against: the most app-like and least distinctive of the three.
Pi: static shadows and solid fills, no blur.
